commit.message:
scd:piv: Allow key import on all cards

* scd/app-piv.c (do_writekey): Do not restrict to YubiKeys.

--

Key import uses the Yubico import command (INS 0xFE), which is not
part of the PIV specification. Other vendors implement it too, for
example Token2, so do not check for a YubiKey before sending it. A
card without the command rejects it, and since the previous commit
the slot then keeps its existing key and public key. On such cards
the error changes from "Not supported" to the error for the status
word returned by the card.

Tested on a TOKEN2 PIN+ R3.3 card in a Cherry ST-2xxx reader (T=0),
slot 9E, and on a Nitrokey 3, slot 95, which holds a P-256 key
generated on the card:

  Card        Import                 Result
  ----------  ---------------------  ----------------------------
  TOKEN2      RSA-2048, RSA-4096     imported; RSA-4096 key signs
  TOKEN2      Ed25519 (scdaemon)     rejected; key kept
  Nitrokey 3  RSA-2048 (card, 6A81)  "Not supported"; key kept

"Key kept" means READKEY still returns the keygrip of the slot's key.
The Nitrokey 3 does not implement the import command.

Signed-off-by: David Seifert <soap@gentoo.org>

commit.message:
gpg: Fix TOFU trust models to actually check UTK signatures.

* g10/tofu.c (signed_by_utk): Add arg ctrl.  Use macros fro the
  sigclass.  Check the signature before returning true.
--

This bug sits here since the introduction of the TOFU models.  It is
just another nail into the coffin of _this_ TOFU implementation.
What we do in gpg is way to complicated and maybe even more complicate
than the WoT it tried to simplify.  One major problem with our
implementation with all its heuristics, is that one may only check a
file once to not mess up the statistics.  This is highly impractical in
real life.  Tofu checking belongs to the caller, for example the
address book of the mail client.

GnuPG-bug-id: 8404
Reported-by: arthur.chan@adalogics.com
Fixes-commit: 8df8aa13c795e400324a782fbaea578c8f2a1398
